extracted.intended_audience: AILA members, immigration attorneys, employers and practitioners who handle H-1B petitions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for submitting public comments to USCIS on the proposed H-1B electronic registration rule, urging delay of implementation and focusing on timing/implementation concerns; includes use of AILA model comment language and a January 2 deadline. Aimed at practitioners and stakeholders to leverage on-the-ground expertise and mobilize submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet the January 2 deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: We have until January 2 to make an impact on this critically important proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments promptly due to the short comment window; act during the holiday period if possible so the collective impact is felt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and customize AILA's model comment
rubrics_metrics.description: AILA has launched a model comment campaign on the proposed H-1B rule... The comment template is very easy to customize and submit following this publicly available link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with AILA's model language and tailor it to your practice/client experience to save time and ensure your comment is aligned with the campaign's ask.

rubrics_metrics.name: Urge USCIS to delay implementation until FY2021 or after beta-testing
rubrics_metrics.description: AILA is asking members to customize and submit a comment urging USCIS to delay implementation of the H-1B registration rule until at least the fiscal year (FY) 2021 H-1B cap season or until a comprehensive, functional and thoroughly beta-tested system can be rolled out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the central ask clear: delay roll-out until a later cap season or until the system is fully tested to avoid disruptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on timing and implementation of the electronic registration system
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the short turnaround time on the regulation, AILA opted to focus the campaign on the timing and implementation of the electronic registration system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize comments about how and when the registration system will be implemented (operational readiness, testing, timelines) though commenters may add other substantive points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain negative impacts on businesses, employers, and prospective H-1B holders
rubrics_metrics.description: These drastic and rushed changes would negatively impact American businesses, employers, and prospective H-1B visa holders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe concrete harms (planning uncertainty, increased anxiety, operational disruption) and how rushed implementation would affect employers and workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide on-the-ground/practitioner expertise and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: We have the on-the-ground expertise to meaningfully comment – please leverage AILA’s impact and submit a comment today.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use your direct experience handling H-1B petitions to give specific examples of how proposed changes would affect workflow, client counseling, and cap-season preparations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage peers to submit comments and share the model
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your own comment and encourage your colleagues to do the same by sharing AILA’s model comment language with your networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amplify impact by mobilizing colleagues and networks to submit individualized comments rather than relying on a single organizational submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult AILA resources for background and context
rubrics_metrics.description: For additional information about the proposed regulation, please see AILA’s resources, including our explaine, practice alert, an earlier Think Immigration blog post, and our QuickTake video on the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review linked resources to inform and support your comment with factual and procedural context; cite relevant AILA materials where helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional: raise other substantive concerns beyond timing/implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the short turnaround time on the regulation, AILA opted to focus the campaign on the timing and implementation of the electronic registration system, however, members are encouraged to weigh in on other aspects of the proposed regulation in their comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have additional substantive objections or suggestions (e.g., selection order changes favoring U.S. master’s degree holders), include them, but note the campaign's primary focus to avoid diluting the central message.
